name: Associate – Foundations

facts.time: 120 minutes, with about 135 minutes of total seat time
facts.passing: 720 on a scaled range of 100 to 1,000
facts.validity: 12 months from the date you earn it

questions.q:
You are a knowledge worker deciding whether to escalate a Claude-generated output. 
Which is the correct order of decision steps?
- Identify the audience and the impact of the output if it is wrong.
- Document the decision and the rationale for traceability.
- Compare the output's risk profile to the organization's escalation criteria.
- Decide whether to use, iterate further, or escalate.
- Assess the output's accuracy, completeness, and any unverified claims.

You are writing system-level instructions for a Project that supports recurring writing tasks. 
Which step should be performed first when writing the system-level instructions?

options.t: Refine the drafted instructions based on observed gaps from validation runs.
Validate the drafted instructions against representative requests for the Project.
Distribute the finalized instructions to collaborators on the Project.
Define the purpose of the Project and the boundaries the instructions must respect.

questions.q:
A knowledge worker is explaining how to use feedback to improve Claude-supported work over time. 
Which description is most accurate?

options.t: Capture general impressions after each run and apply them as broad prompt rewrites, since broad rewrites cover more potential issues than targeted changes.
Capture feedback as an aggregate quality score per run, since aggregate scores show whether quality is improving without requiring detail on individual issues.
Capture specific feedback after each run, translate it into targeted prompt or workflow changes, and observe whether subsequent runs improve.
Capture feedback only after several runs so patterns emerge from the volume of observations, then apply changes based on the patterns rather than any single run.

questions.q:
You are an operations assistant asking Claude to summarize 200 weekly metric records across multiple regions. 
Which output format communicates the data most clearly?

options.t: a structured table with one record per row and one metric per column, sorted by region
a narrative summary organized by region, describing trends and notable records in prose
a series of regional narrative briefs, each describing weekly performance in paragraph form
a bulleted list of observations grouped by region without consistent metrics across entries

questions.q:
An analyst has been asked to compute summary statistics from an uploaded sales data file and produce a chart for a weekly report. 
Which output approach best fits the task?

options.t: Use Code Execution to perform the calculations and generate the chart, then verify the computed results against the source data before sharing the output.
Request a narrative description of the data in the chat response without computing values, leaving the summary statistics and the chart unproduced and the weekly report incomplete.
Ask Claude to estimate the summary statistics from a brief preview of the file, accepting unverified figures rather than running the calculations against the full uploaded dataset.
Produce a written placeholder for the chart in the chat response without generating the actual visualization, leaving the weekly report without the visual output it requires.

questions.q:
An operations assistant is using Claude to support process optimization for an existing intake workflow. 
The assistant has access to the current process documentation and recent cycle-time data. 
Which activity best uses Claude to support this process optimization task?

options.t: Use Claude to interview each team member who works on the intake process and synthesize the interview output into a redesigned workflow.
Map the current intake process, identify likely bottlenecks based on the cycle-time data, and propose optimization options for human review.
Apply Claude to predict the cycle-time impact of each proposed change and rank them so the team can implement improvements in priority order.
Generate an optimized version of the intake process based on industry benchmarks, then compare it to the current process to identify gaps.

questions.q:
A knowledge worker is explaining the purpose of an organizational Al governance tramework to a colleague. 
Which description is most accurate?

options.t: A governance framework documents the Al policies the organization is legally required to adopt, focusing on regulatory compliance rather than day-to-day use.
A governance framework defines the training every employee must complete before using Al tools, with separate equirements for each tool the organization licenses.
A governance framework lists the Al tools the organization licenses and the cost of each, so users can pick the most cost-effective tool for each task.
A governance framework defines approved tools, allowed data, required reviews, and reporting paths so Al is used consistently and accountably.

questions.q:
You are organizing connected data sources for a team and must complete the planning steps before authorizingany connection. 
Which two planning steps must be completed BEFORE authorizing a new Connector? (Select two.) Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.t: Decommission any unused legacy Connectors that may still be authorized.
Migrate every existing report off the prior data source onto the new Connector.
Confirm the data classification of the source and the team's permission to use it.
Confirm the Connector is on the approved-vendor list maintained by IT.
Train every team member on the new Connector through formal training sessions.

questions.q:
An HR associate is preparing to use Claude on a sensitive personnel matter. 
The organization's Al policy explicitly states that information related to ongoing investigations must not be entered into Al tools. 
Which response best aligns with the policy?

options.t: Enter the investigation-related information into Claude only after the investigation closes, since the policy applies during the investigation period.
Enter a paraphrased version of the investigation-related information that removes identifying details, since paraphrasing addresses the spirit of the policy.
Enter the investigation-related information into Claude in an Incognito chat, since Incognito chats do not retain information and therefore fall outside the policy's intent.
Refrain from entering investigation-related information into Claude and consult HR leadership for an approved alternative way to handle the matter.

questions.q:
You are an operations lead mapping production tasks to Claude model strengths to set realistic expectations. 
Which two production tasks fit Claude's strengths most clearly? (Select two.) Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.t: synthesizing a single executive summary across many long source documents
monitoring a live sensor data stream and flagging anomalies as they occur in real time
drafting a tone-and-audience-aware customer-facing email under human review
issuing a binding legal determination based solely on Claude's analysis of case documents
calculating the precise settlement value of a derivative contract using live market inputs

questions.q:
You are configuring a new Claude Project for a specific recurring workload 
Which Project configuration step should be performed first?

options.t: Add reference materials and instructions that the Project will rely on.
Invite collaborators to the Project and confirm the appropriate access levels.
Test the configured Project on a representative request from the workload.
Define the purpose of the Project and the recurring tasks it must support.

questions.q:
You are a knowledge worker who decomposed a "draft a board memo" request into fifteen tiny steps and noticed the output now feels disjointed because related ideas were split apart. 
Which adjustment is most appropriate?

options.t: Remove all sequencing so the steps run in random order.
Consolidate related steps into fewer cohesive sections that group naturally connected ideas.
Combine the original request back into one unstructured sentence.
Subdivide each tiny step into ten more tiny steps for additional precision.

questions.q:
A knowledge worker often switches between Claude and another Al service while working on a long-running project. 
Which Claude feature most directly reduces repetitive context-setting between sessions?

options.t: Rely on a single static Artifact pasted into each chat as the only continuity mechanism, ignoring the Memory feature that is purpose-built for retaining work-relevant context across sessions.
Disable Memory entirely and re-paste the same context paragraphs at the start of every Claude session, even though Memory is designed to retain that context across conversations automatically.
Open every Claude session in Incognito mode, which prevents the conversation from contributing to Memory and therefore eliminates the cross-session continuity the project would benefit from.
Enable Memory and use the import capability to bring relevant context from the other Al service into Claude as a starting point for the project's work.

questions.q:
You are a project lead reviewing a teammate's habit of using the same prompt template for every task regardless of type. 
Which feedback is most warranted?

options.t: The habit is ideal because a single template guarantees consistent quality across all task types.
The prompting strategy should be adapted to each task type because one template does not produce equally strong outputs across all tasks.
The prompting strategy should not change between tasks because adapting it wastes time and adds no value.
Task type has no effect on the appropriate prompting strategy.

questions.q:
You received a vague request to "look at our pricing." 
After discovery, the goal is confirmed: produce a structured competitor-pricing summary the team can act on, not new pricing ideas. 
Which strategy best fits the clarified task?

options.t: Use a comparative analysis strategy that contrasts the company's pricing against a single named competitor, since pairwise comparison produces the clearest output.
Use a divergent brainstorming approach to generate a wide range of possible competitor-pricing observations, then narrow to the most likely ones.
Use an open conversational strategy that explores competitor pricing iteratively across several prompts, allowing the structure to emerge from the conversation.
Use a research strategy that gathers structured information about competitor pricing, names sources, and notes confidence in each finding.

questions.q:
You are an HR specialist reviewing data items proposed for inclusion in a Claude prompt. 
Which two data items are appropriate to include in a Claude prompt for a routine task? (Select two.) Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.t: A redacted job description that the model will adapt for a posting.
Accommodation request notes from an employee's HR file needed to draft a role-adjustment memo.
Employee identification numbers and hire dates for the team roster included to help Claude personalize onboarding communications.
A compensation-band summary that includes employee names and current salary figures for a specific team.
An anonymized summary of an HR policy that the model will rephrase.

questions.q:
You are a marketing manager using Claude to ideate concepts for a campaign and must complete the framing steps before generating concepts. 
Which two framing steps must be completed BEFORE asking Claude to generate concepts? (Select two.) Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.t: Review the Claude-generated concepts and select the two strongest for further development.
Define the brand voice and the audience the concepts will address.
Define the goal of the campaign and its success metrics.
Select a finalist concept and prepare it for stakeholder approval.
Schedule the campaign launch and rollout dates with the agency.

questions.q:
You are a product designer using Claude in a solution-design exercise. 
Which solution-design step should be performed first when using Claude?

options.t: Generate candidate solution concepts using Claude across diverse styles.
Produce detailed mock-ups of the chosen solution for stakeholder review.
Compare the candidate concepts against the constraints and select a finalist.
Articulate the problem the solution must address and the constraints in play.

questions.q:
You are a customer-success manager considering whether to escalate a Claude-generated response. 
Which factor most strongly raises the impact of the output and supports escalation before external use?

options.t: The response is an internal draft summarizing the associate's notes from a customer call for their own reference.
The response is a brief internal announcement about an upcoming team all-hands meeting.
The response is an unchanged draft for a paying customer that includes a service-level commitment.
The response is a casual rephrasing of an internal team status update.

questions.q:
You are reviewing a Claude-generated report whose tone is confident throughout. 
Which question best separates plausibility from verification?

options.t: Can each specific claim be traced to a credible source or to the supplied input material?
Does the response cover the topic comprehensively based on its length and section count?
Does the response open with a clear, well-framed statement of the main finding?
Does the response use varied sentence structure across sections?

questions.q:
A Claude associate is incorporating reviewer feedback that named two specific issues with a Claude-drafted brief. The rest of the brief was accepted as written. 
Which next step is most likely to produce a strong revision?

options.t: Address the two specific issues and also revise unrelated sections to maintain a consistent voice across the brief after the edits.
Rewrite the briet trom scratch incorporating the two specific issues, since starting tresh integrates the teedback more cleanly than targeted edits.
Address the two specific issues directly, leave unrelated parts unchanged, and document the changes for the next review.
Address the two specific issues and add a third improvement the associate identified, since combining reviewer feedback with self-identified improvements is more efficient.

questions.q:
You are a communications manager validating a Claude-generated newsletter that includes a specific industry growth figure. 
The figure appears in three trade-press articles, but none of them link to the underlying study. 
Which validation step is correct?

options.t: Accept the figure because three trade-press articles repeat it.
Remove the source attribution and present the figure as common knowledge.
Locate the original study referenced by the trade-press articles and verify the figure in the primary source.
Use the highest figure across the three articles to make the newsletter more compelling.

questions.q:
You are a process consultant integrating Claude into an existing weekly workflow. 
Which is the correct order of integration steps?
- Pilot the integrated workflow with a small group and gather feedback.
- Document the current workflow steps, owners, and decision points.
- Update the documented workflow and roll it out to the broader team.
- Identify the steps where Claude can augment work and where humans must remain.
- Define the inputs Claude needs, the outputs Claude returns, and the hand-offs around each step.

You are an operations assistant selecting a model for a recurring meeting-summary task that does not require deep reasoning and runs at moderate volume. 
Which selection best balances cost, speed, and quality?

options.t: Haiku, which is suitable only when the task requires the fastest possible turnaround.
Opus, which prioritizes depth at higher latency and rate-limit consumption.
Sonnet, which provides solid quality at moderate latency and rate-limit consumption for everyday work.
A custom model, which the Associate-level user would need to build and train independently.

questions.q:
An HR business partner is configuring two separate Projects for two distinct client engagements. 
Which configuration best prevents context bleed between the two engagements?

options.t: Set up each Project with its own distinct memory context, knowledge sources, and instructions, and verify that information from one Project does not appear in the other Project's responses.

Use a single shared Project for both client engagements with combined memory, knowledge sources, and tructions, on the assumption that Claude will keep the two clients' contexts separate without configuration.

Configure both Projects to share the same memory context to reduce setup effort, even though shared memory between unrelated client engagements is precisely the configuration that produces context bleed.
Skip Project configuration entirely and use general chats for both engagements, which provides no scoped nemory contexts and offers no structural separation between the two clients' work streams.

questions.q:
You are reviewing a Claude-generated competitor brief for unsupported claims. 
Which is the correct order of review steps?
- Cross-check each specific claim against the supplied source material or trusted external references.
- Decide whether to correct, re-prompt, or escalate based on the findings.
- Document each unsupported or inconsistent claim with its location and severity.
- Identify the specific factual claims, statistics, and citations in the brief.
- Read the brief from beginning to end and flag any claims that feel surprising.

A business analyst has been asked to use Claude to extract requirements from a recorded stakeholder interview transcript. 
The transcript is approximately 90 minutes long and covers multiple topics. 
Which approach is most likely to produce a usable structured output?

options.t: Provide the transcript along with a structured prompt that requests must-haves, nice-to-haves, open questions, and conflicts as separate sections.
Provide the transcript and ask Claude to produce a single ranked list of requirements, since a single list is easier for stakeholders to review than separate sections.
Provide the transcript and ask Claude to summarize it; extract requirements from the summary in a second pass since two passes catch more detail.
Provide the transcript and ask Claude to produce a chronological list of every statement that contains a verb, then classify each statement as a requirement or not.

questions.q:
A senior manager is reviewing a colleague's habit of never updating their team's Project configurations because "if it works once, it works forever.' " 
Which feedback is most warranted?

options.t: Configurations should be updated only when output quality visibly degrades, since proactive updates risk introducing regressions in working configurations.
Configurations should be left alone if the team is satisfied with current outputs, and any required updates should be handled at the chat level rather than the Project level.
Configurations should be reviewed and updated periodically because policies, terminology, and source documents change over time, even when output quality has not visibly degraded.
Configurations should be updated on a fixed schedule regardless of whether the underlying policies and source documents have changed, since regular maintenance prevents drift.

questions.q:
You are an analyst reviewing a Claude response that addresses two of three required questions and skips the third. 
Which prompt element most likely needs strengthening?

options.t: The context provided to Claude should be expanded with additional background detail about the subject matter.
The output format should be revised to allow Claude to determine the appropriate structure for each question's answer.
The role assigned to Claude should be changed to a more specialized expert persona to increase response depth.
The task statement should explicitly enumerate the three required questions and require an answer to each.

questions.q:
You are a Claude associate troubleshooting a recurring poor output. 
Which is the correct order of diagnostic steps? 
(1) Form a hypothesis about which prompt element most likely caused the deficiency. 
(2) Apply a single targeted change and observe the effect on the output. 
(3) Read the output end to end and identify the specific deficiency. 
(4) Compare the deficient output to the prompt to spot mismatches between input and output. 
(5) Document the root cause and the resolution for future reference.

A finance consultant is adapting a Claude-generated narrative for a quarterly investor update. 
Investors have a fixed time window for the call and expect the headline result and forward outlook to be clear early. 
Which adaptation is most appropriate for this audience?

options.t: Lead with the quarter's operational highlights, present the financial result in the middle for context, and close with the forward outlook.
Lead with the forward outlook, since investors are most interested in what comes next, and present the headline result and drivers afterward.
Lead with the headline result, present the key drivers concisely, and close with the forward outlook.
Lead with a chronological recap of the quarter's events, present the headline result at the natural end of the recap, and conclude with the forward outlook.

questions.q:
You are a bank manager presented with a request to use Claude as the sole decision-maker on customer credit- line approvals. 
Which response is most appropriate?

options.t: Accept the sole-decision-maker design because Claude can process applications faster than a human review team.
Implement the design on a pilot basis and notify compliance only if issues arise during production use.
Decline the sole-decision-maker design and propose Claude assisting analysts who retain decision authority.
Expand the design so Claude both evaluates applications and issues final approval notices to customers directly.

questions.q:
You are a research associate preparing inputs for a long task that references two lengthy regulatory documents, but only specific sections apply. 
Which approach best preserves context-window capacity?

options.t: Extract only the relevant sections from each document and include those, omitting unrelated chapters.
Paste the full text of both documents without trimming to maximize the available material.
Split each document into one-character pieces and provide them one at a time.
Skip the documents entirely and rely on Claude to invent the missing context.

questions.q:
A finance manager must select a Claude feature for a task that requires deterministic calculations across a multi- tab spreadsheet. 
Which selection best fits the requirement?

options.t: Use a standard chat prompt for the calculations, which generates text without running code and does not produce the reproducible computational output the multi-tab calculation task requires.
Use the Research feature for the calculations, which gathers and synthesizes external sources and is not the appropriate feature for deterministic computation on an uploaded spreadsheet.
Use an Artifact alone for the calculations, which provides a stable editable surface for the result but does not perform the deterministic computation that Code Execution would run.
Use Code Execution, which runs code in a sandbox to perform calculations on the uploaded file and produce outputs the associate can verify.

questions.q:
You are a business analyst evaluating a Claude-generated business case against the agreed acceptance criteria. 
Which is the correct order of evaluation steps? 
(1) Compare the business case with the source data and required topics. 
(2) Document gaps and inaccuracies for follow-up or correction. 
(3) Restate the acceptance criteria for the business case. 
(4) Decide whether to use the business case, iterate, or escalate. 
(5) Read the business case from beginning to end to form an initial impression.

An support representative is configuring a Project for drafting customer-facing apology emails after service outages. 
The current custom instructions tell Claude to "be empathetic and casual, keep it short, and offer a goodwill credit." 
The customer-service team has flagged that recent drafts have been too brief, have offered goodwill credits in cases where policy does not allow them, and have used contractions that the brand voice guide prohibits. 
Which adjustment best aligns the configuration to the use case?

options.t: Replace "be empathetic and casual" with "match the brand voice guide," remove the instruction to offer goodwill credits, and let each draft determine its own length based on the incident.

Move the brand voice guide and the goodwill-credit policy into the Project knowledge base and rely on the documents alone to govern tone, length, and credit decisions, without changing the custom instructions.

Specify the brand voice attributes (empathetic, formal, no contractions), set a minimum length, and instruct Claude to recommend a goodwill credit only when the attached eligibility policy permits one.
Keep the existing instructions and add a sentence telling Claude to consult the brand voice guide and the goodwill-credit policy that are attached to the Project knowledge base.

questions.q:
You are a refining a prompt over several iterations. 
The output drifts further from the requested template with each change. 
Which step is most appropriate?

options.t: Discard all prior versions and start with no record of what worked.
Continue making large simultaneous changes until the output happens to align.
Revert to the version of the prompt that produced the closest match and adjust from that baseline.
Stop iterating and accept the most off-target version.

questions.q:
You are a communications specialist preparing to describe Claude's role in a workflow to multiple stakeholder groups and must complete the preparation steps before drafting messages. 
Which two preparation steps must be completed BEFORE drafting the stakeholder messages? (Select two.) Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.t: Archive the drafted messages in the corporate communications repository.
Identify the stakeholder groups and what each group needs to understand.
Define the key facts about Claude's role and the boundaries that apply.
Send the drafted messages out and gather feedback for revision.
Schedule a follow-up forum to handle questions raised by the messages.

questions.q:
You are a marketing manager using Claude to research a new market segment. 
Which research step should be performed first?

options.t: Generate a final research report combining every Claude output produced.
Submit a series of Claude prompts to gather information across the segment.
Validate the gathered information against authoritative external sources.
Define the specific research questions that must be answered for the segment.

questions.q:
A Claude associate is identifying the bottleneck in a content workflow that takes too long to publish. 
The workflow has five steps: 
- research, 
- drafting, 
- internal review, 
- legal review, 
- and publication. There is cycle-time data for each step from the past month. 
Which signal most directly identifies the bottleneck?

options.t: The step with the longest queue or the largest backlog of items waiting to enter it.
The step where individual contributors report the highest workload in their weekly status updates.
The step with the highest average cycle time per item across the past month's runs.
The step most recently added to the workflow, based on the assumption that process changes introduce the most friction.

questions.q:
You are a knowledge worker summarizing common prompt failure patterns for the team. 
Which battern most often produces vadue or off-taraet outout?

options.t: A prompt that names a topic but does not state the task, audience, or required output structure.
A prompt that explicitly names the role, task, audience, and required output format.
A prompt that includes a representative example of the desired output.
A prompt that adds clear constraints on length and tone.

questions.q:
A project lead is evaluating a Claude-generated status report against the project charter. 
The report will be delivered to a steering committee, which expects accurate status against committed milestones. 
Which set of criteria provides the strongest evaluation frame?

options.t: Readability, narrative flow, and whether the report tells a coherent story about the project's progress.
Speed of generation, visual presentation quality, and consistency with the formatting used in previous status reports.
Length, formatting consistency, and tone appropriateness for a steering committee audience.
Accuracy of facts against the charter, completeness against required reporting fields, and relevance to the audience receiving the report.

questions.q:
You are a project manager weighing workflow steps by how much leverage Claude integration provides. 
Which workflow step typically offers the greatest Claude leverage in a knowledge-work team?

options.t: approving final deliverables for external publication without further review
negotiating contractual terms with external parties on behalf of the company
drafting and synthesizing across many sources for a downstream reviewer
making final personnel decisions about hiring, promotion, or termination

questions.q:
You are an operations lead and notice that a Project's outputs have been drifting from the team's current expectations. 
Which maintenance action should be tried first?

options.t: Retire the Project and rebuild a new one from scratch with fresh content.
Switch the Project to a different Claude model in the hope it behaves better.
Review the Project's instructions and reference materials against current standards.
Continue using the Project and accept the drift as the new baseline of behavior.

questions.q:
You are a customer-success lead running an interactive workflow where each turn must respond quickly and the per-turn reasoning is light. 
Which selection best aligns with the requirements?

options.t: Choose Haiku to keep latency low and to handle a light reasoning load efficiently at scale.
Choose a model based on the alphabetical order of its name.
Choose any model because latency does not vary by model.
Choose Opus to maximize reasoning depth despite higher latency.

questions.q:
You are sorting Claude output structural defects by which most undermines clarity. 
Which structural defect most severely undermines the clarity of the output?

options.t: A single subheading is shorter than the other subheadings in the document.
Two adjacent paragraphs present the same information using inconsistent terminology.
Typographic inconsistencies appear throughout multiple sections of the document.
The main conclusion contradicts the evidence presented in the body.

questions.q:
You are reviewing items proposed for inclusion in a Project that supports policy summaries. 
Which two items are appropriate to include in the Project? (Select two.) Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.t: the summary format and the audience expectations the summaries must meet
the current policy library that the summaries are drawn from
presentation slides from a recent team training session on internal communication standards
active client case files maintained by a separate legal team for a different workstream
employee onboarding records used in a separate HR workflow managed by the same team

questions.q:
A manager is deciding what changes to make while conducting a Memory maintenance review for a long-running workflow. 
Which two actions best support Memory quality over time? (Select two.)

options.t: Delete all memories as the maintenance action to ensure a clean slate, then allow Claude to rebuild context organically through subsequent workflow runs.
Export the current memories as a backup before making changes, so prior context can be restored if a maintenance edit unintentionally removes information the workflow still depends on.
Leave all memories untouched on the basis that the workflow has been running consistently and no output- quality issues have been reported.
Disable Memory entirely to eliminate the risk of stale entries surfacing in future workflow runs.
Identify and edit or delete entries that are stale, inaccurate, or no longer relevant, and add context Claude has not utomatically captured but the workflow continues to need.

questions.q:
You are a content creator. A first response from Claude is accurate but uses inconsistent terminology that does not match your organization's glossary. 
Which iterative change addresses the issue most directly?

options.t: Increase the requested length so the inconsistent terminology appears more often.
Ask Claude to invent additional terms unrelated to the glossary.
Remove the topic from the prompt to avoid the terminology issue entirely.
Provide the organization's glossary and instruct Claude to use only those terms throughout the response.

questions.q:
Before sharing a Claude-generated brief, an analyst is applying the Al Fluency Framework Discernment competency to evaluate it. 
Which review best reflects Discernment principles?

options.t: Accept the brief on the basis that it reads fluently and the subject matter aligns with the analyst's professional knowledge of the topic.
Skip the source material check during review and rely on overall tone and logical flow as proxies for factual accuracy.
Review the opening paragraph and the conclusion of the brief, since these sections typically reflect the quality of the full document.
Conduct a systematic check of the brief against the task requirements, source material, and professional standards before sharing it.

questions.q:
An associate is responding to an executive who claims that Claude will eliminate the need for any human review on customer-facing content. 
The executive is the budget approver for the team's Al tools. 
Which response is most appropriate?

options.t: Escalate the executive's claim to a senior leader outside the team before responding directly, since the issue affects more than just the associate's team.
Pilot the executive's proposal on a low-risk subset of customer-facing content first, and use the pilot resultsto make the case for retaining human review on higher-risk content.
Defer to the executive's authority and remove the human review step from customer-facing content, monitoring the results closely for the first several weeks.
Acknowledge the productivity gains, then explain that human review remains essential on customer-facing content because of accuracy and brand risk, with specific examples.

questions.q:
You are evaluating a Claude output that appears to contain hallucinated content. 
Which response step should be performed first when a hallucination is suspected?

options.t: Discard the entire output and regenerate the output with a fresh prompt.
Document the hallucination pattern in the team's risk register for future reference.
Notify the user community that the output contains a hallucinated claim.
Pinpoint the specific claim that appears to be unsupported by available evidence.

questions.q:
You are a project manager reviewing Claude usage approaches that teammates have proposed for a project workflow. 
Which two workflow steps are well-suited for Claude support? (Select two.) Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.t: approving a final external press release without any human review
issuing legally binding contractual commitments on behalf of the company
deciding promotion outcomes for staff based solely on the model's judgment
synthesizing a literature review across many uploaded research documents
drafting a structured project status update from a set of meeting notes

questions.q:
You are using Claude to redesign an employee onboarding workflow and must complete the high-level decomposition steps before specifying detailed artifacts. 
Which two decomposition steps must be completed BEFORE specifying exact email content and the schedule? (Select two.) Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.t: Pilot the onboarding workflow with a small cohort of new hires.
Identify the major phases of the onboarding experience.
Negotiate the onboarding budget with the finance department.
Define the overall objective of the onboarding experience.
Roll out the onboarding workflow to every new hire across the company.

questions.q:
You are optimizing a recurring Claude workflow and must complete the diagnostic steps before changing the worktlow. 
Which two diagnostic steps must be completed BEFORE changing the recurring workflow? (Select two.) Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.t: Notify executive leadership of the projected savings from the optimization.
Identify the steps that contribute most to time, cost, or quality issues.
Deploy the updated workflow across the team and monitor for adoption issues.
Measure the current workflow's quality, time, and cost across recent runs.
Document the revised workflow steps and update the team's standard operating procedures.

questions.q:
You are a project manager reviewing stakeholder messages that teammates have drafted about Claude's role in a workflow. 
Which two messages are appropriate for stakeholder communication about Claude? (Select two.) Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.t: A claim that Claude will handle every task without any human involvement
A claim that the model never makes errors and requires no quality review
An honest description of where Claude assists and where humans retain decisions
A clear statement of the limits and known failure modes of the integration
A vague reassurance that "the Al is taking care of it" without further detail

questions.q:
A learning specialist is configuring a Claude Project for a recurring course-design workflow. 
Which configuration approach best leverages a Skill alongside other Project elements?

options.t: Configure the Project with custom instructions that contradict the Skill's documented purpose, creating ambiguity about which guidance Claude should follow within the recurring course-design workflow.
Add the relevant Skill to the Project, upload the supporting knowledge sources, and write custom instructionsthat reterence both the Skill and the knowledge.
Upload the supporting knowledge sources but disable the relevant Skill, eliminating the packaged capability the workflow needs and forcing each chat to reconstruct the procedure manually.
Add the Skill to the Project but omit the supporting knowledge sources and any custom instructions, so the Project lacks the reference content and persistent guidance the workflow requires.

questions.q:
A customer-success team member is reviewing a Claude-generated customer health-check report against the agreed deliverable list. 
The report covers all five required topics, but the renewal-risk section names only one risk factor where the deliverable specification calls for renewal risk to be assessed across pricing, product fit, and stakeholder change. 
Which conclusion is best supported?

options.t: The report's completeness cannot be assessed from the deliverable specification alone; the customer should review the output and confirm whether the renewal-risk depth is sufficient.
The report does not meet the deliverable specification because a section that addresses only one of three required risk dimensions counts as a missing section.
The report meets the deliverable specification because all five required topics appear and the renewal- risk section is present in the output.
The report meets the topic-level requirements but the renewal-risk section is under-scoped against the specification and should be expanded before delivery.

questions.q:
An operations assistant is redesigning a recurring data-processing workflow step to use Code Execution. 
Which two design choices best support reliable integration? (Select two.)

options.t: Standardize the input file format the step expects, so each Code Execution run receives consistent input and produces comparable, verifiable output across recurring weekly cycles.
Vary the input file format from run to run to accommodate the different source systems that supply the data each week.
Embed the Code Execution step inside the workflow without documenting the expected output format or the fields it produces.
Eliminate the human review step that follows Code Execution, since the sandboxed environment already verifies that the code ran without errors.
Define a brief output-verification step in which a human reviewer confirms the computed result against an expected range or sanity check before the output advances to downstream consumers.

questions.q:
You are a Claude associate running an ethics review on a Claude-assisted deliverable before publication. 
Which is the correct order of review steps? 
(1) Confirm that transparency requirements are met for the audience receiving the deliverable. 
(2) Document the review outcome and any changes made. 
(3) Identify the audience and the potential impact of the deliverable on that audience. 
(4) Make targeted revisions or escalate if a concern requires more authority to resolve. 
(5) Examine the content for unsupported generalizations, fairness concerns, and accuracy issues.

A knowledge worker is explaining the cost, speed, and quality trade-offs across Claude models to a colleague. 
Which generalization correctly describes the trade-off?

options.t: More capable models generally consume less of the usage limit because their reasoning is more efficient,even though they run more slowly than lighter models.
More capable models generally consume more resources and run more slowly, while lighter models areusually taster and less expensive.
Lighter models consume more resources per request than more capable models because they always requiremultiple passes to match higher-model quality.
Speed and resource consumption are independent of model capability; the difference between Haiku, Sonnet,and Opus is reasoning depth alone.

questions.q:
The first output from Claude is partially useful but has tone and detail issues. 
Which two refinement actions are most likely to produce a meaningfully better output? (Select two.) Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.t: Add a specific tone descriptor and a concrete audience to the prompt.
Provide an example of an output that meets the desired standard.
Resubmit the same prompt several times and select the best response.
Append the phrase "please do better" to the end of the original prompt.
Increase the temperature setting and resubmit the unchanged prompt.

questions.q:
You are an HR specialist reviewing model choices made by colleagues for various tasks. 
Which two model choices represent appropriate matches between the model and the task? (Select two.) Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.t: a higher-capability model selected solely because it is the most expensive option
a higher-capability model for one-line keyword extraction at high request volume
a higher-capability model for complex multi-step legal reasoning under review
a lighter, faster model for nuanced multi-document strategic synthesis
a lighter, faster model for routine FAQ-style replies under tight latency budgets

questions.q:
You are an HR specialist sorting potential ethical risks of a Claude-supported workflow. 
Which two risks pose the highest ethical concern in an HR-adjacent workflow? (Select two.) Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.t: a clerical typo in a routine internal calendar invitation
decisions that materially affect a person's employment without human accountability
inconsistent tone and formatting across internal HR communications sent to employees
outputs that systematically disadvantage members of a protected group
inconsistent use of the company's preferred dash style across documents

questions.q:
You are a knowledge worker reviewing a Claude-generated brief that asserts a "well-known industry standard" without naming any source. 
How should this assertion be handled?

options.t: Strengthen the assertion by adding more confident wording.
Republish the brief unchanged because the claim sounds authoritative.
Accept the assertion because the phrase "well-known" is reassuring.
Treat the assertion as unverified, and either source it from an authoritative reference or remove it.

questions.q:
You are a business analyst deciding which output-formatting and context-window practices to recommend to teammates. 
Which two practices represent effective use of the context window? (Select two.) Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.t: Reuse the same context block across multiple requests to avoid rebuilding it each time.
Paste full email threads related to the project into the context so the model has the complete conversational history.
Concatenate all source documents end-to-end with no separators between them.
Trim irrelevant material before submitting the request to keep the context focused.
Use clear section headers to separate different parts of the input material.

questions.q: Claude turns a response into a separate Artifact rather than an inline chat reply mainly when the content is:

options.t: Substantial, self-contained, and reusable
A response that simply runs past a few paragraphs of prose
Written in a formal, professional tone
Generated during an active Research session

questions.q:
A Pro-plan user avoids Haiku 4.5 entirely, believing it is only a lesser model for people who cannot access better ones. 
Which statement corrects this?

options.t: Haiku 4.5 is offered mainly to Free-plan users as an entry-level option
Haiku 4.5 is best reserved for tasks needing the deepest reasoning
Haiku 4.5 produces the highest-quality reasoning of the four
Haiku 4.5 is the deliberate choice for quick, high-volume tasks

questions.q:
A business user is unsure which model to pick for typical everyday writing and analysis. 
According to Anthropic's guidance, which model is the recommended default?

options.t: Opus 4.8, reserved for complex high-stakes reasoning
Haiku 4.5, the fastest and lightest model
Sonnet 5, the balanced default for most work
Fable 5, the newest and most capable model

questions.q: For external-facing or sensitive content, Anthropic recommends disclosing Al involvement in addition to which other safeguard?

options.t: Qualified professional review before it reaches consumers
Switching to the account's strongest available model
Attaching citations to the generated draft for source traceability
Turning off the model-improvement training toggle

questions.q:
Regenerating the same prompt gives you three noticeably different values for a key metric across three tries. You need a single reliable number for a finance summary due to leadership today. 
Given the inconsistency across regenerations, what is the most appropriate action?

options.t: Pick the value that appeared in two of the three tries
Use whichever value is closest to what you already expected
Average the three values and report the resulting mean figure
Treat the inconsistency as a warning; verify the source data

questions.q:
A team plans to run a Research session for every routine status question in a daily workflow. 
What is the key cost consideration they should weigh?

options.t: Research runs on a separate budget that does not touch message limits
Research is unavailable on paid plans for daily use
Research consumes usage quota faster than a normal message
Research lowers the account's usage limit ceiling for the rest of the day

questions.q:
A strategist needs both careful reasoning and heavy multi-source gathering for a detailed market-entry analysis. 
Which combination does the guidance support for this task?

options.t: Neither is needed, since a single Web Search covers everything
Brainstorming alone, since ideation naturally includes reasoning and sources
Research combined with Extended Thinking for reasoning plus source-gathering
Concise Style, which balances depth and brevity for you

questions.q:
One section of a long Markdown document in an Artifact needs a tone change for a different audience, while the rest is correct. 
What is the most appropriate way to revise it?

options.t: regenerate the entire document from scratch with a new prompt
start a new conversation and rebuild the whole document
highlight the section and request a targeted edit of that part
retry the original prompt to generate an alternate full version

questions.q:
A prompt that has produced excellent results all week returns one oddly disorganized answer. The user believes the prompt itself is fine. 
What is the best first move?

options.t: Use Retry to regenerate a fresh answer to the prompt
Rewrite the prompt from scratch to prevent future errors
Switch to a more capable model for this request
Start a brand-new conversation and re-explain the whole task

questions.q:
You're briefing stakeholders on where Claude's output needs extra scrutiny. 
Which single category should you tell them to always check against an authoritative primary source before use?

options.t: Formatting and layout choices in a routine internal draft memo
Brainstormed lists of rough, early-stage project ideas
Statistics, legal claims, citations, and direct quotes
Minortone adjustments applied to a casual internal team message

questions.q: Which of the following features lets a user build an interactive working mockup that iterates in its own side panel?

options.t: Styles, which set tone and format per conversation
Memory, which synthesizes background insights automatically
Web search, which returns quick factual lookups
Artifacts, which hold reusable, iterable content separately

questions.q:
You enabled a custom Skill and a colleague worries it will bloat every prompt the way project instructions do. 
Which fact reassures them?

options.t: A Skill is injected into every prompt like instructions
A Skill overrides profile instructions across the whole account
A Skill can be created only by an org administrator
A Skill loads only when Claude judges the task relevant

questions.q:
With the Gmail connector active, a user asks Claude to prepare a reply to a vendor. 
Before actually creating that draft, the connector requires:

options.t: A one-time authorization that covers later email actions
The user's explicit approval for that specific draft action
Admin sign-off before a reply draft can be generated
Nothing further, since the connector itself was already enabled

questions.q:
A business user gets a vague, unhelpful first draft from Claude. 
According to Anthropic's guidance, what does an effective prompt most reliably need?

options.t: The most capable model paired with a high effort setting
Explicit context, a specific task, and output format
Forceful, capitalized wording that demands compliance
A single sweeping instruction covering the whole task

questions.q: Within a single Project, which mechanism makes uploaded material available to every chat in that Project?

options.t: The Project knowledge base, shared across all chats
The conversation content of any one chat in the Project
The Project description field entered when creating the Project
A Custom Style applied to the current conversation only

questions.q:
Your conversation context has grown long, and the model is producing inconsistent outputs. 
Which context-management step should be performed first?

options.t: Summarize the prior conversation into a concise statement of the current state.
Start a fresh conversation and repaste only the essential prior context.
Continue the existing conversation and hope the model recovers consistency.
Switch to a different model in the hope that the new model handles long context better.

questions.q:
You are setting up a Connector for a shared data source that several colleagues will use. 
Which Connector setup step should be performed first?

options.t: Document the Connector's purpose and the appropriate use cases for the team. ab
Use the Connector in a representative task to evaluate its real-world utility. ab
Connect the data source and confirm the authentication is working as expected.
Confirm the Connector is approved and the data classification is appropriate.ab

questions.q: Which SIAM process is responsible for restoring a service that has been degraded or interrupted?

options.t: incident management
event management
measuring and monitoring
problem management

questions.q:
A knowledge worker is preparing to use the Gmail connector with Claude for the first time. 
Which statement most accurately describes the connector's behavior at the user level?

options.t: Claude searches and reads emails the user has access to and labels them according to user-defined rules, with reply drafting handled in a separate workflow.
Claude searches and reads emails the user has access to and drafts replies for the user to send manually, with each action requiring explicit user approval.
Claude searches and reads emails the user has access to in a read-only mode, and the user must compose any reply manually outside the connector.
Claude searches and reads emails the user has access to and sends replies on the user's behalf for low-risk messages, with higher-risk messages routed to the user for approval.

questions.q:
You are a Claude associate troubleshooting a Claude response that introduces facts not present in the supplied source. 
Which root cause is most directly indicated?

options.t: The prompt asks Claude to act as a researcher rather than a writer.
The prompt's heading-based structure encourages Claude to generate placeholder content under each heading even when the source doesn't cover it.
The prompt does not constrain Claude to use only facts present in the supplied source.
The prompt asks for a comprehensive response, which leads Claude to fill perceived gaps with plausible- sounding but unverified detail.

questions.q:
An analyst is working in a long Claude conversation. The conversation contains roughly 60 turns covering an initial requirements analysis, several rounds of data review, and a current drafting phase. Recent responses have started to drift from the agreed requirements. 
Which step most directly addresses the drift while preserving the analyst's progress?

options.t: Move the source data and the requirements into a Project knowledge base, then continue the drafting work in a new chat inside that Project.
Switch the conversation to a model with a larger context window so the accumulated history no longer causes drift and continue without restructuring the inputs.
Open a new chat and paste only the current draft, then continue refining it there without the prior requirements and data-review context.
Summarize the agreed requirements, the key data findings, and the current draft state, then continue in the same chat by reasserting the summary as the working context.

questions.q:
You are a solution architect designing a Claude-based assistant with access to 60 internal tools across multiple business domains. Loading every tool definition on every request increases token usage and time to first response. 
Which design pattern best addresses this issue without sacrificing capability breadth?

options.t: Increase the maximum context length so all 60 tool definitions fit within a single request without exceeding the limit.
Apply progressive tool discovery so a curated initial subset is exposed and additional tools are loaded on demand based on the task.
Group the 60 tools into five fixed categories and load one category per request based on a static mapping of task type to category.
Use a separate model call to condense all 60 tool definitions into a compact index that is prepended to each user turn for tool selection.

questions.q:
You are a platform architect designing an internal Claude-based assistant that serves both finance analysts and external auditors. Each population must access only documents permitted by their role. 
Where should role-based access control be enforced in the pipeline?

options.t: after the response is generated, by post-filtering content that should not have been retrieved
at the retrieval layer, before any role-restricted content reaches the prompt construction step or the model
inside the system prompt as a natural-language instruction that names the specific role-based access groups Claude should treat as unauthorized
at the retrieval layer, but relying on a single organization-wide access token shared across all roles rather than per-role scoping

questions.q:
You are selecting the documentation set that should accompany a Claude-based deployment at handoff. 
Which set is most complete?

options.t: the original design proposal, its review comments, meeting notes from design sessions, and the approved requirements document
a project retrospective document, a lessons-learned summary, and a list of contributors
architecture overview, ADRs, component-level diagrams, runbooks for common operations, on-call playbook, and a list of known limitations
user-facing release notes, a marketing one-pager describing the deployment, and a customer FAQ

questions.q:
When refining a Claude output that does not meet expectations. 
Which iterative refinement step should be performed first?

options.t: Submit the revised prompt and capture the new output.
Compare the new output against the original criteria.
Identify the specific weaknesses in the current output.
Modify the prompt to address each identified weakness.

questions.q:
A knowledge worker has noticed that the same prompt for a recurring weekly task produces inconsistent outputs across runs. Some weeks the output uses the right sections but the wrong tone, other weeks the tone is right but a section is missing. The source inputs change each week but follow the same structure. 
Which cause is most worth investigating first?

options.t: The model is non-deterministic, so identical prompts naturally produce different outputs even when the prompt itself is well-written, and the team should accept the variation.
The recurring prompt under specifies the audience, tone, format, and required sections, so each run drifts depending on what the model emphasizes that turn.
The team should split the prompt into separate prompts for tone and structure, since combining both in one prompt produces the mixed inconsistency the team is seeing.
The source inputs vary too much from week to week, and the team should standardize the inputs before changing the prompt.

questions.q:
Preparing an AI-assisted work product for external delivery, a senior manager is applying the AI Fluency Framework Diligence competency. 
Which step best reflects Diligence principles?

options.t: Deliver the work product without independent verification on the basis that AI assistance shifts accountability away from the human, even though Diligence holds the human fully accountable for the output.

Delegate accountability for the AI-assisted work product to Claude itself rather than retaining it as a human obligation, contrary to the Diligence principle that humans remain accountable for AI-assisted outputs.
Skip verification of any element on the assumption that fluent output implies accuracy, even though Diligence requires the human to verify and correct AI-assisted outputs before they are acted upon.
Identify the elements of the work product that must be independently verified or corrected before delivery, and take ownership of those verifications as a professional accountability obligation.v

questions.q:
You are reviewing claims about prompt iteration that colleagues have made in a recent training. 
Which two claims about prompt iteration are accurate? (Choose two.) Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.t: Repeated resubmission of the same prompt is the most reliable way to improve output.
Output comparison against original criteria validates whether iteration helped.
Iteration is most productive when each change targets a specific diagnosed weakness.
Iteration should stop only after every possible alternative phrasing has been tried.
More iterations always produce a better output regardless of what was changed.

questions.q:
A Claude associate is reviewing a Claude-drafted set of customer-segment descriptions for an internal marketing brief. One description applies a generalization about a demographic group’s purchasing behavior that does not hold for individual customers in the segment. 
Which response is most appropriate?

options.t: Revise the description to focus on observed behaviors rather than generalizations about people, and validate the revision against actual customer data.
Remove the entire customer-segment description from the brief, since any segmentation that involves demographic characteristics is likely to introduce similar issues.
Keep the description as written for the internal brief, since internal use does not carry the same risk as external publication of demographic generalizations.
Add a disclaimer to the description, noting that the generalization may not apply to all individuals in the segment, and keep the underlying description unchanged.

questions.q:
You are running an optimization pass on a recurring workflow. 
Which is the correct order of optimization steps? 
(1) Apply targeted optimization to the bottleneck step 
(2) Roll out the optimized workflow to the broader team and document the change 
(3) Identify the bottleneck step using measured time per step and queue length 
(4) Map the current workflow steps, owners, and decision points 
(5) Pilot the change with a small group and measure the effect against the prior baseline

As part of a workflow redesign, a process analyst is applying the AI Fluency Framework Delegation competency. 
Which two criteria most directly inform Delegation decisions? (Choose two.)

options.t: The reversibility of the task and the consequence of an error, which together indicate whether the step is safe to delegate to Claude or should be retained for human decision-making.
The need for human creativity, empathy, or judgment in the step, which indicates whether the task is appropriate for AI delegation or requires the human capabilities Claude cannot provide.
The visual complexity of the workflow diagram, since steps with more connections and dependencies are more likely to require human oversight.
The seniority of the team member who currently performs the step, since more senior roles typically involve higher-stakes tasks that warrant human retention.
The length of time the workflow has existed in its current form, since well-established processes have been sufficiently validated for AI delegation.

questions.q:
A Claude associate is evaluating whether to enable a Skill that was provided by an unfamiliar third party. 
Which two checks best support a sound trust decision? (Choose two.)

options.t: Verify the source of the Skill against the organization’s approved-Skill list before enabling it within claude.ai or any Project the team uses for its work.
Treat the Skill's appearance in a public listing as sufficient validation, without confirming the source, the requested permissions, or alignment with the organization’s approved-Skill list.
Skip permission review on the assumption that the Skill cannot exceed the boundaries of the workflow, even though Skills can request access that the task does not require.
Review the permissions and capabilities the Skill requests and confirm that the requested access is appropriate for the task the Skill is intended to perform.

Enable the Skill immediately on the basis of strong external reviews, even though the source has not been validated against the organization’s approved-Skill list and the permissions remain unverified.

questions.q: A knowledge worker is defining what "workflow optimization" means at the Associate level for the team's recurring AI-supported workflows. Which description is most accurate?

options.t: Reducing the number of steps in the workflow to the smallest possible count, since fewer steps mean faster cycle time and lower error rates.
Reducing redundancy, removing low-value steps, and applying Claude where it adds measurable value, while keeping required reviews and quality gates.
Replacing manual steps with Claude-supported steps wherever possible, since each replacement adds value by reducing the time the team spends on the workflow.
Standardizing every step of the workflow to a fixed template so each run produces identical output, without adjusting for variation in the workflow's inputs.

questions.q:
You are a Claude associate assessing a proposed Claude use case before approving it for your team. 
Which is the correct order of assessment steps? 
(1) Compare the use case against the organization’s policies and the relevant regulatory considerations. 
(2) Document the assessment outcome and the rationale for traceability. 
(3) Identify the audience, decision impact, and reversibility of the outputs. 
(4) Decide whether the use case proceeds, requires modification, or is declined. 
(5) Identify the data types involved and whether sensitive data is implicated.

You are reviewing colleagues’ responses to feedback received on Claude-drafted communications. 
Which two feedback responses are productive? (Choose two.) Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

incorporating all feedback received, including contradictory suggestions, into the next draft simultaneously
deferring all feedback to a later revision cycle to avoid disrupting the current draft’s consistency
asking clarifying questions when feedback is ambiguous before acting on it

labeling each workflow step with descriptive names to improve readability for new team members
extracting the standard reference material into a Project to avoid repeating it
reorganizing the workflow document’s section headings to improve navigation
adding a quality check on outputs before they enter the downstream process

questions.q:
A project manager is transforming a Claude-generated draft into a polished board memo.

Which set of refinements is most appropriate?

Apply consistent headings, expand each section to give the board full context, and align terminology with the organization's standards.
Tighten wording for executive scanability and verify each fact against source data; leave heading structure and terminology as written to preserve the draft’s voice.
Apply consistent headings and align terminology with the organization’s standards; rely on Claude’s verification of facts, since the draft was generated from the source data.

questions.q:
You are an operations lead evaluating prompting strategies that teammates have proposed for various task types. 
Which two strategies represent appropriate matches between strategy and task type? (Choose two.) Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.t: rigid templated prompting for early-stage creative naming and tagline ideation
open exploratory prompting for legal contract redlining against a clause library
open exploratory prompting for early-stage strategic brainstorming on a new market
rigid templated prompting for casual customer-feedback summarization with no schema
rigid templated prompting for monthly compliance reports against a fixed schema

questions.q:

options.t: Define the quality bar, the latency tolerance, and the expected request volume.
Retest the selected model whenever a new model version is released.
Choose a candidate model based on the requirements profile and known capabilities.
Promote the selected model to production traffic for the workload.
Sign off on the production rollout plan with the platform and security teams.

questions.q:
You are an operations manager preparing a quick reference card for a team. 
Which description correctly characterizes the three Claude model tiers in general terms?

options.t: Haiku is the most capable model for the deepest reasoning, while Opus is the lightweight model for quick replies
All three models offer the same reasoning depth and differ only in response speed and cost.
Haiku is fast and lightweight, Sonnet is the balanced default for most everyday work, and Opus is the most capable for complex reasoning at higher latency and cost.
Sonnet is the fastest of the three models because its architecture is optimized for speed rather than reasoning depth.

questions.q:
You are a project manager working through a long planning conversation with Claude and must keep the conversation productive as it grows. 
Which two practices keep a long planning conversation productive? (Choose two.) Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.t: Open a new thread for every minor follow-up question to keep threads short.
Restate constraints and goals when the focus shifts to a new subtopic.
Periodically summarize decisions made so far to compress the working state.
Switch context aggressively between unrelated planning topics within one thread
Avoid summarizing so the model retains every original word it has produced.

questions.q:
A finance manager is about to discuss a confidential pre-announcement figure with Claude. 
Which two settings best align with sound privacy practice for this conversation? (Choose two.)

options.t: Skip the privacy setting decision and proceed with default behavior, since the conversation will not explicitly instruct Claude to remember the figure.
Disable Memory contribution for the conversation if Incognito mode is not used, so the confidential figure is not retained as persistent context that could surface in later unrelated sessions.
Treat the conversation as appropriate for default Memory settings, since the figure will only be discussed briefly and is unlikely to be retained.
Enable Memory contribution for the conversation so the context carries forward to support follow-up analysis in future sessions.
Open the conversation in Incognito mode, which prevents the conversation from contributing to Memory and avoids persistent retention of the confidential pre-announcement figure across sessions.

questions.q:
You have iterated a Claude prompt eight times, and the output quality has plateaued for the last four attempts. 
Which conclusion is most appropriate?

options.t: Iteration should stop and the current output should be accepted as-is regardless of remaining issues.
Iteration should stop and the task should be abandoned without communicating to stakeholders.
Iteration has reached diminishing returns and the next step is human review or a different approach.
Iteration should continue indefinitely because more attempts always improve quality.

questions.q:
You are running a weekly feedback-and-adjustment cycle. 
Which is the correct order of cycle steps? 
(1) Translate feedback into one or two targeted adjustments for the next cycle. 
(2) Run the next cycle and compare results against the prior cycle. 
(3) Capture the specific feedback received during the review. 
(4) Document what changed, what effect it produced, and any remaining issues. 
(5) Decide whether to continue iterating, switch approach, or escalate.

You are a knowledge manager structuring source material in the context window for a long Claude evaluation task. 
Which two practices produce a more effective use of the context window? (Choose two.) Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.t: Paste every available document into context regardless of relevance to the task.
Mark each source clearly with delimiters so the model can attribute claims correctly.
Repeat the same instruction at the start, middle, and end to reinforce it.
Mix sources together in a single block so the model can synthesize them freely.
Place the most reference-critical material near the beginning or end of context.

questions.q:
An HR business partner is configuring a new Project for recurring policy questions from managers.

Which content belongs in the Project knowledge base?

options.t: the current employee handbook plus prior versions of the handbook going back five years, so Claude can answer questions about how policies have changed
the current employee handbook, the leveling guide, the policies-FAQ, and every email the HR team has sent about policy in the past year, for additional context
the current employee handbook only, with the leveling guide and the policies-FAQ attached at the start of each chat as needed for that chat’s topic
the current employee handbook, the leveling guide, and the policies-FAQ document referenced across the Project’s chats

questions.q:
A knowledge worker is briefing a stakeholder group on Claude's limitations. 
The stakeholders will use Claude on customer-facing work where confident- sounding output that contains errors would cause real harm. 
Which limitation is most important to communicate clearly?

options.t: Claude’s responses vary across runs of the same prompt, so stakeholders should run each prompt several times and compare outputs before using any single response.
Claude can produce confident-sounding output that contains unsupported claims, so human review remains essential for high-impact work.
Claude can produce long, detailed responses that take time to read, so stakeholders should request shorter outputs when working under tight deadlines.
Claude’s knowledge has a training cutoff, so stakeholders must verify any time-sensitive claims against current sources before using them.

questions.q:
You are a knowledge worker preparing inputs for a Claude prompt. 
Which data type most clearly requires extra handling such as redaction or anonymization before being included in the prompt?

options.t: public press releases the company has already published
customer government identifiers and full payment-card numbers tied to named individuals
job titles taken from the company’s public organizational chart
generic product descriptions available on the company’s marketing site

questions.q:
Before sharing a Claude-generated brief, an analyst is applying the AI Fluency Framework Discernment competency to evaluate it. 
Which review best reflects Discernment principles?

options.t: Accept the brief on the basis that it reads fluently and the subject matter aligns with the analyst’s professional knowledge of the topic.
Skip the source material check during review and rely on overall tone and logical flow as proxies for factual accuracy.
Review the opening paragraph and the conclusion of the brief, since these sections typically reflect the quality of the full document.
Conduct a systematic check of the brief against the task requirements, source material, and professional standards before sharing it.

questions.q:
A project manager is defining how Claude can support requirements analysis for an upcoming engagement. Their team will conduct stakeholder interviews and review existing process documentation as part of discovery.

options.t: Use Claude to generate a complete requirements list from the project name and a short description, since requirements for similar engagements are largely standard.
Use Claude to prioritize the requirements the team has already gathered, leaving the gathering itself to manual analyst work since prioritization is more time-consuming.
Use Claude to synthesize stakeholder inputs and existing process documentation into a structured list of requirements with traceability to each source.

questions.q:
An account manager has used Claude to extract requirements from stakeholder notes.
